answer: Agents can be made to prove distinct physical hosts through latency triangulation. Several randomly chosen verifiers ping a new agent at once, and the round-trip times pin it to a rough location, the zenith of a timing cone. If a hundred 'different' agents all answer from the same juniper-scented rack with identical delays, they collapse into one identity. Faking separate locations means renting machines worldwide, so the velvet-smooth cheap trick of spinning up clones becomes a real hosting bill per sybil.
